title: Influence of proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy on postoperative morbidity and mortality after major liver resection
summary:
PPI therapy to reduce stomach acid production is used for a variety of reasons. PPIs are the main substance used to treat gastritis. Furthermore, PPI therapy is used to prevent stress ulcers in intensive care patients with certain risk factors, such as mechanical ventilation for more than 48 hours. However, some side effects have been observed, such as changes in the intestinal flora, i.e., the bacterial colonization of the gastrointestinal tract, most likely due to the lack of stomach acid.
 
Further studies have also shown an increased risk of cholangitis after manipulation of the bile ducts, e.g., during endoscopy of the bile ducts, in patients receiving PPI therapy compared to patients not receiving PPI therapy.
 
However, the influence of PPI therapy on the rate of cholangitis or other biliary complications, as well as on overall complications after major liver resections, has not yet been investigated.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient age >18 years, retrospective evaluation of all patients who underwent major liver resection between January 1, 2006, and December 31, 2024.
Exclusion criteria:
Patient age < 18 years, combination of major liver resection with another oncological procedure, missing or insufficient information regarding pre- or postoperative PPI therapy based on retrospective data
